results.title: Frobenius group with given kernel and complement
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For subgroups $F$ and $H$ of a group $G$, $G$ is a Frobenius group with kernel $F$ and complement $H$ (Kourovka 6.53) if $G = F \rtimes H$ (that is, $F$ is normal in $G$, $F \cap H = 1$ and $FH = G$), $F \ne 1$, $H \ne 1$, $H \cap gHg^{-1} = 1$ for every $g \in G \setminus H$, and the non-trivial elements of $F$ are exactly the elements of $G$ that lie in no conjugate $gHg^{-1}$ of $H$.

results.title: Kourovka Problem 20.96 (periodic Frobenius groups)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The statement, posed by A. I. Sozutov, that for every group $G$ in which every element has finite order and every normal abelian subgroup $A$ of $G$ that is neither trivial nor all of $G$ and such that for every $a \in A$ with $a \ne 1$ the centralizer $C_G(a)$ of $a$ in $G$ is contained in $A$, there are subgroups $F$ and $H$ of $G$ such that $G$ is a Frobenius group with kernel $F$ and complement $H$.

results.title: Lytkina–Mazurov theorem on periodic Frobenius groups
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a group in which every element has finite order, and let $A$ be a normal abelian subgroup of $G$ that is neither trivial nor all of $G$ and such that for every $a \in A$ with $a \ne 1$ the centralizer $C_G(a)$ of $a$ in $G$ is contained in $A$. results.title: Polynomial evaluation commutes with the Frobenius power
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Evaluating `p` at `x ^ q` equals the `q`-th power of evaluating `p` at `x`, where `q` is the cardinality of the finite field `F`.

results.title: Mahler measure of an integer polynomial
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The Mahler measure of $f \in \mathbb{Z}[X]$ is the Mahler measure of its image in $\mathbb{C}[X]$. It equals $|a| \prod_i \max(1, |\alpha_i|)$, where $a$ is the leading coefficient of $f$ and the $\alpha_i$ are the complex roots of $f$ counted with multiplicity.

results.title: Nonzero integer polynomials have Mahler measure at least one
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If $f \in \mathbb{Z}[X]$ is a nonzero polynomial, then its Mahler measure satisfies $M(f) \ge 1$.

results.title: Mahler measure of a monic linear integer polynomial
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every integer $a$, the Mahler measure of the integer polynomial $X - a$ is $\max(1, |a|)$.

results.title: Mahler measure of $X - 1$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The integer polynomial $X - 1$ has Mahler measure $1$.

results.title: Mahler measure of $X - 2$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The integer polynomial $X - 2$ has Mahler measure $2$.

results.title: Mahler measures above one
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: This is the set of real numbers of the form $M(f)$, where $f \in \mathbb{Z}[X]$ is an integer polynomial whose Mahler measure $M(f)$ is strictly larger than $1$.

results.title: Lehmer's constant
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Writing $M(f)$ for the Mahler measure of an integer polynomial $f$, Lehmer's constant is $C_{40a} = \inf \{M(f) : f \in \mathbb{Z}[X],\ M(f) > 1\}$, the infimum of the Mahler measures of integer polynomials that are strictly larger than $1$.

results.title: Lehmer's constant bounds every Mahler measure above $1$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every integer polynomial $f$ whose Mahler measure is strictly larger than $1$, Lehmer's constant is at most the Mahler measure of $f$.

results.title: Lehmer's constant is at least one
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Lehmer's constant $L$, the infimum of the Mahler measures strictly larger than $1$ of polynomials in $\mathbb{Z}[X]$, satisfies $1 \le L$.

results.title: Lehmer's constant is at most $2$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Lehmer's constant $C_{40a}$ satisfies $C_{40a} \le 2$.

results.title: Lehmer's question
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The proposition that there are integer polynomials with Mahler measure arbitrarily close to $1$ from above: for every real $\varepsilon > 0$ there is a polynomial $f \in \mathbb{Z}[X]$ whose Mahler measure $M(f)$ satisfies $1 < M(f) < 1 + \varepsilon$.

results.title: Lehmer's question in terms of Lehmer's constant
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Lehmer's constant equals $1$ if and only if Lehmer's question has a positive answer, that is, for every $\varepsilon > 0$ there is an integer polynomial whose Mahler measure lies strictly between $1$ and $1 + \varepsilon$.

results.title: Lehmer's polynomial
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Lehmer's polynomial is the integer polynomial $X^{10} + X^9 - X^7 - X^6 - X^5 - X^4 - X^3 + X + 1$.

results.title: Smyth's polynomial
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Smyth's polynomial is $X^3 - X - 1 \in \mathbb{Z}[X]$.

results.title: Reciprocal polynomial
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: An integer polynomial $f$ is reciprocal when reversing its coefficients gives $f$ or $-f$, that is, when $X^d f(1/X) = f$ or $X^d f(1/X) = -f$, where $d$ is the degree of $f$, taken to be $0$ when $f = 0$.

results.title: Mahler measure of Lehmer's polynomial
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The Mahler measure of Lehmer's polynomial is at most $1176281/1000000 = 1.176281$.

results.title: Lehmer's upper bound for Lehmer's constant
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Lehmer's constant is at most $1176281/1000000 = 1.176281$.

results.title: Smyth's theorem for nonreciprocal polynomials
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f \in \mathbb{Z}[X]$ be an integer polynomial that is not reciprocal and whose constant term $f(0)$ is nonzero. Then the Mahler measure of $f$ is at least the Mahler measure of Smyth's polynomial $X^3 - X - 1$.

results.title: Zero part of a divisor
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a divisor $D$ on a set of points $C$, the zero part $D^+$ of $D$ is the divisor on $C$ whose coefficient at each point $P \in C$ is $\max(D(P), 0)$.

results.title: Pole part of a divisor
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a divisor $D$ on a set of points $C$, the pole part $D^-$ of $D$ is the divisor on $C$ whose coefficient at each point $P \in C$ is $\max(-D(P), 0)$.

results.title: Coefficients of the zero part
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every divisor $D$ on a set of points $C$ and every point $P \in C$, the coefficient at $P$ of the zero part $D^+$ of $D$ is $\max(D(P), 0)$.

results.title: Coefficients of the pole part
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every divisor $D$ on a set of points $C$ and every point $P \in C$, the coefficient at $P$ of the pole part $D^-$ of $D$ is $\max(-D(P), 0)$.

results.title: The zero part of a divisor is effective
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every divisor $D$ on a set of points $C$, the zero part $D^+$ of $D$ is effective: $D^+(P) \ge 0$ for every point $P \in C$.

results.title: The pole part of a divisor is effective
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every divisor $D$ on a set of points $C$, the pole part $D^-$ of $D$ is effective: $D^-(P) \ge 0$ for every point $P \in C$.

results.title: A divisor is its zero part minus its pole part
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every set of points $C$ and every divisor $D$ on $C$, let $D^+$ be its zero part, with coefficient $\max(D(P), 0)$ at each point $P$, and $D^-$ its pole part, with coefficient $\max(-D(P), 0)$ at each point $P$. Then $D^+ - D^- = D$.

results.title: Genus of a smooth proper curve
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a field $k$ and a curve $C$ over $k$, that is, a $k$-scheme that is proper, smooth of relative dimension $1$ and geometrically irreducible, the genus of $C$ is a natural number.

results.title: Jacobian of a smooth proper curve
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a field $k$ and a curve $C$ over $k$, that is, a $k$-scheme that is proper, smooth of relative dimension $1$ and geometrically irreducible, the Jacobian $J(C)$ of $C$ is a $k$-scheme.

results.title: The Jacobian has dimension equal to the genus
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $C$ be a proper, smooth, geometrically irreducible curve over a field $k$. The Jacobian $J(C)$ is smooth of relative dimension $g$ over $k$, where $g$ is the genus of $C$.

results.title: Abel–Jacobi map
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $C$ be a proper, smooth, geometrically irreducible curve over a field $k$. Each $k$-rational point $P$ of $C$ gives a morphism of $k$-schemes $C \to J(C)$ from $C$ to its Jacobian, the Abel–Jacobi map based at $P$.

results.title: The Abel–Jacobi map sends the base point to zero
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $C$ be a proper, smooth, geometrically irreducible curve over a field $k$, let $J(C)$ be its Jacobian, and let $P$ be a $k$-rational point of $C$. The Abel–Jacobi map $C \to J(C)$ based at $P$ sends $P$ to the identity point of $J(C)$ for its group scheme structure.

results.title: Universal property of the Jacobian
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $C$ be a proper, smooth, geometrically irreducible curve over a field $k$, let $J(C)$ be its Jacobian, let $P$ be a $k$-rational point of $C$, and let $\iota_P : C \to J(C)$ be the Abel–Jacobi map based at $P$. Let $A$ be a group scheme over $k$ that is smooth, proper and geometrically irreducible. For every morphism of $k$-schemes $f : C \to A$ sending $P$ to the identity point of $A$, there is a unique…

results.title: Group law on the rational points of the Jacobian
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $C$ be a proper, smooth, geometrically irreducible curve over a field $k$. The commutative group structure on the set of $k$-rational points of the Jacobian $J(C)$ is the one induced by its commutative group scheme structure: the product of two $k$-points $x$ and $y$ is $\mu \circ (x, y)$, where $\mu$ is the multiplication morphism of $J(C)$.

results.title: Uniform Mordell–Lang constant
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For natural numbers $g$ and $d$, $c(g, d)$ is a natural number: the constant in the uniform bound on rational points of curves in Theorem 1.1 of Dimitrov, Gao and Habegger.

results.title: The uniform Mordell–Lang constant is at least one
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For all natural numbers $g$ and $d$, the uniform constant satisfies $c(g, d) \ge 1$.

results.title: Uniform Mordell–Lang for curves
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $g \ge 2$ and $d \ge 1$ be natural numbers, let $F$ be a number field with $[F : \mathbb{Q}] \le d$, and let $C$ be a proper, smooth, geometrically irreducible curve over $F$. results.title: Klartag's lattice packing theorem
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There is a real constant $c > 0$ such that for every integer $n \ge 1$ there is a linear map $\varphi : \mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{R}^n$ for which the ellipsoid $E = \varphi(B)$, the image of the open Euclidean unit ball $B$ about the origin, has volume exactly $c n^2$ and the origin is the only point of $E$ whose coordinates are all integers.

results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $K$ be a field, let $a$ and $b$ be finite multisets of elements of $K$ (the upper and lower parameters), and let $n$ be a natural number. The $n$-th generalized hypergeometric coefficient is

results.title: Generalized hypergeometric series
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $K$ be a field and $A$ a topological ring that is a $K$-algebra. For finite multisets $a$ and $b$ of elements of $K$, the generalized hypergeometric series is the formal multilinear series on $A$ whose $n$-th term is the $n$-linear map $(x_1, \dots, x_n) \mapsto c_n \, x_1 x_2 \cdots x_n$, where $c_n \in K$ is the $n$-th generalized hypergeometric coefficient with upper parameters $a$ and lower parameters $b$.

results.title: Admissible lower parameters
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A finite multiset $B$ of complex numbers is admissible as lower parameters if no element of $B$ is $0$ or a negative integer, that is, $-k \notin B$ for every natural number $k$.

results.title: Summability of the generalized hypergeometric series
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: For finite multisets $a$ and $b$ of complex numbers and $z \in \mathbb{C}$, the generalized hypergeometric series with upper parameters $a$ and lower parameters $b$ is summable at $z$ if the family $(c_n z^n)_{n \ge 0}$ is summable in $\mathbb{C}$, where $c_n$ is the $n$-th generalized hypergeometric coefficient.

results.title: Generalized hypergeometric function
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For finite multisets $a$ and $b$ of complex numbers and $z \in \mathbb{C}$, the value ${}_pF_q(a; b; z)$, where $p = |a|$ and $q = |b|$, is the sum $\sum_{n \ge 0} c_n z^n$, where $c_n$ is the $n$-th generalized hypergeometric coefficient with upper parameters $a$ and lower parameters $b$.

results.title: Rising factorials at admissible lower parameters are nonzero
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $B$ be a finite multiset of complex numbers that is admissible as lower parameters. Then for every $b \in B$ and every natural number $n$, the rising factorial $(b)_n = b(b+1)\cdots(b+n-1)$, with $(b)_0 = 1$, is nonzero.

results.title: Terminating generalized hypergeometric series are summable
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $a$ and $b$ be finite multisets of complex numbers, and let $c_n$ be the $n$-th generalized hypergeometric coefficient with upper parameters $a$ and lower parameters $b$. If $-N \in a$ for some natural number $N$, then for every $z \in \mathbb{C}$ the family $(c_n z^n)_{n \ge 0}$ is summable, that is, the generalized hypergeometric series with these parameters is summable at $z$.

results.title: Strict local minimum
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $f \colon X \to Y$ be a function from a topological space $X$ to a set $Y$ equipped with a relation $<$. Then $f$ has a strict local minimum at a point $a \in X$ if $f(a) < f(x)$ for all $x \ne a$ in some neighborhood of $a$.

results.title: Strict local maximum
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $f \colon X \to Y$ be a function from a topological space $X$ to a set $Y$ equipped with a relation $<$. Then $f$ has a strict local maximum at a point $a \in X$ if $f(x) < f(a)$ for all $x \ne a$ in some neighborhood of $a$.

results.title: A strict local minimum is a local minimum
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f \colon X \to Y$ be a function from a topological space $X$ to a preordered set $Y$. If $f$ has a strict local minimum at $a \in X$, then $f$ has a local minimum at $a$, that is, $f(a) \le f(x)$ for all $x$ in some neighborhood of $a$.

results.title: A strict local maximum is a local maximum
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f \colon X \to Y$ be a function from a topological space $X$ to a preordered set $Y$. If $f$ has a strict local maximum at $a \in X$, then $f$ has a local maximum at $a$, that is, $f(x) \le f(a)$ for all $x$ in some neighborhood of $a$.

results.title: Negation turns a strict local minimum into a strict local maximum
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $X$ be a topological space and let $Y$ be an additive group with a relation $<$ such that addition on the left and addition on the right are strictly monotone. If $f \colon X \to Y$ has a strict local minimum at $a \in X$, then $x \mapsto -f(x)$ has a strict local maximum at $a$.

results.title: Negation turns a strict local maximum into a strict local minimum
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $X$ be a topological space and let $Y$ be an additive group with a relation $<$ such that addition on the left and addition on the right are strictly monotone. If $f \colon X \to Y$ has a strict local maximum at $a \in X$, then $x \mapsto -f(x)$ has a strict local minimum at $a$.

results.title: Strict second-derivative test, minimum version
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ and $x_0 \in \mathbb{R}$. If $f''(x_0) > 0$, $f'(x_0) = 0$, and $f$ is continuous at $x_0$, then $f$ has a strict local minimum at $x_0$.

results.title: Strict second-derivative test, maximum version
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ and $x_0 \in \mathbb{R}$. If $f''(x_0) < 0$, $f'(x_0) = 0$, and $f$ is continuous at $x_0$, then $f$ has a strict local maximum at $x_0$.

results.title: Stationary random functions (Slutsky–Khinchin)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\mu$ be a measure on a measurable space $\Omega$, and let $v$ assign to each real $t$ a function $v_t : \Omega \to \mathbb{R}$. Then $v$ is stationary if there are a real number $c$ and a function $R : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ such that for all real $t$ and $h$, $\int v_t \, d\mu = 0$, $\int v_t^2 \, d\mu = c$ and $\int v_t \, v_{t+h} \, d\mu = R(h)$.

results.title: The antiholomorphic quadratic map
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For $c \in \mathbb{C}$, the map $T_c : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ is $T_c(z) = \bar z^2 + c$, where $\bar z$ is the complex conjugate of $z$.

results.title: The Mandelbar set (tricorn)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The Mandelbar set is the set of $c \in \mathbb{C}$ for which the orbit of $0$ under the map $T_c(z) = \bar z^2 + c$ is bounded: there is a real number $M$ with $|T_c^n(0)| \le M$ for all $n \ge 0$, where $T_c^n$ is the $n$-th iterate of $T_c$ and $T_c^0$ is the identity.

results.title: The Mandelbar set is not path-connected
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The Mandelbar set (tricorn), the set of $c \in \mathbb{C}$ for which the orbit of $0$ under $z \mapsto \bar z^2 + c$ is bounded, is not path-connected.

results.title: Number of overpartitions
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $n$, $\overline{p}(n)$ is the number of overpartitions of $n$, that is, of pairs consisting of a partition $p$ of $n$ and a set of overlined part sizes, each of which occurs as a part of $p$. For example, $\overline{p}(3) = 8$.

results.title: Number of non-overlined copies of a part size
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For an overpartition $O$ of $n$ and a natural number $a$, the number of non-overlined parts of size $a$ in $O$ is the multiplicity of $a$ in the underlying partition of $O$, minus $1$ if $a$ is overlined in $O$ and minus $0$ otherwise.

results.title: Minimal excludant of an overpartition with a multiplicity bound
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For natural numbers $r \ge 1$ and $n$ and an overpartition $O$ of $n$, $\overline{\mathrm{mex}}_r(O)$ is the least positive integer $k$ that occurs fewer than $r$ times among the non-overlined parts of $O$. Such a $k$ exists, since $n + 1$ is not a part of $O$. For $r = 0$, which the paper does not use, the value is $0$ by convention.

results.title: Three-colored distinct-part partitions
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $n$, $D_3(n)$ is the number of triples $(A, B, C)$ of subsets of $\{1, \dots, n\}$ such that the sum of the elements of $A$, the sum of the elements of $B$ and the sum of the elements of $C$ add up to $n$. Here $A$, $B$, $C$ are the parts of the three colors of a partition of $n$ whose parts of each color are distinct.

results.title: The number of overpartitions of zero
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The number $\overline{p}(0)$ of overpartitions of $0$ equals $1$: the empty overpartition is the only one.

results.title: Three-colored distinct-part partitions of $0$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The number $D_3(0)$ of partitions of $0$ into parts of three colors, with the parts of each color distinct, equals $1$: the empty partition is the only one.

results.title: Three-colored distinct-part partitions of $1$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The number $D_3(1)$ of partitions of $1$ into parts of three colors, with the parts of each color distinct, equals $3$: the single part $1$ takes one of the three colors.

results.title: Three-colored distinct-part partitions of $2$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The number $D_3(2)$ of partitions of $2$ into parts of three colors, with the parts of each color distinct, equals $6$: the single part $2$ in one of three colors, or two parts $1$ in two different colors.

results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\sigma\overline{\mathrm{mex}}(n)$ be the sum, over all overpartitions $\pi$ of $n$, of $\overline{\mathrm{mex}}(\pi)$, the least positive integer that does not occur among the non-overlined parts of $\pi$. Then $\sigma\overline{\mathrm{mex}}(n) \sim e^{\pi\sqrt{n}} / (8 n^{3/4})$ as $n \to \infty$, that is, the ratio of the two sides tends to $1$.

results.title: Peak descents
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $l$ be a finite sequence of up steps $U$ and down steps $D$. A peak of $l$ is a position where a step $U$ is immediately followed by a step $D$. The peak descents of $l$ form the list that has, for each peak from left to right, the length $j$ of the maximal run of consecutive steps $D$ that starts at the $D$ of that peak, so that the peak and its descent form the primitive block $U D^j$.

results.title: Peak descents of a sample Dyck path
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The Dyck path $UUUUDDDUDDUUDUUDDD$, which factors as $U\,U\,U\,(UD^3)(UD^2)\,U\,(UD)\,U\,(UD^3)$, has four peaks $UD$, and the lengths of the maximal runs of $D$ steps starting at the $D$ of each peak are, from left to right, $3, 2, 1, 3$.

results.title: Independent set in a hypergraph
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $H$ be a finite hypergraph, that is a finite family of finite sets of vertices, called its edges. A finite set $I$ of vertices is independent in $H$ when no edge $e$ of $H$ satisfies $e \subseteq I$.

results.title: Independence unfolded
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A finite set $I$ of vertices is independent in a finite hypergraph $H$ if and only if no edge $e$ of $H$ satisfies $e \subseteq I$.

results.title: Every set is independent in the empty hypergraph
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Every finite set of vertices is independent in the empty hypergraph, the hypergraph with no edges.

results.title: Subsets of independent sets are independent
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If a finite set $I$ of vertices is independent in a finite hypergraph $H$ and $J \subseteq I$, then $J$ is independent in $H$.

results.title: When the empty set is independent
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a finite hypergraph $H$, the empty set is independent in $H$ if and only if every edge of $H$ is nonempty.

results.title: Steiner triple system
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A finite hypergraph $H$ on a vertex type $V$, that is a finite family of finite subsets of $V$, is a Steiner triple system when it is $3$-uniform (every edge of $H$ has exactly $3$ elements) and any two distinct vertices $u \ne v$ of $V$ lie together in exactly one edge of $H$.

results.title: Steiner triple systems are 3-uniform
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If $H$ is a Steiner triple system, then $H$ is $3$-uniform: every edge of $H$ has exactly $3$ elements.

results.title: Pairs in a Steiner triple system
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If $H$ is a Steiner triple system on a vertex type $V$, then for all vertices $u \ne v$ of $V$ there is exactly one edge $e$ of $H$ with $u \in e$ and $v \in e$.

results.title: Unique element of a singleton family
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $t$ be a finite set of vertices and let $P$ be a property of finite sets of vertices. If $t$ satisfies $P$, then there is exactly one finite set $e$ of vertices with $e \in \{t\}$ and $P(e)$.

results.title: Number of descents of a permutation of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a permutation $w$ of $\{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$, read as the word $w(0)\,w(1) \cdots w(n-1)$, the number of descents $d(w)$ is the number of indices $i$ with $i + 1 < n$ and $w(i) > w(i+1)$.

A linear extension of $P$ is a permutation $w$ of the labels such that $a < b$ whenever $R(w(a), w(b))$, that is, a word $w(0)\,w(1) \cdots w(n-1)$ listing every label once with $w(a)$ before $w(b)$ whenever $R(w(a), w(b))$. The $W$-polynomial is the integer polynomial…

results.title: Neggers' conjecture
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For every $n$ and every relation $R$ on the labels $\{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$ that is naturally labeled, meaning that $R(i, j)$ implies $i < j$, every complex zero of the $W$-polynomial $W(P, x)$ of the poset $P$ generated by $R$ is real.

results.title: Neggers' conjecture is false
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There exist $n$ and a naturally labeled relation $R$ on the labels $\{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$, one in which $R(i, j)$ implies $i < j$, such that the $W$-polynomial $W(P, x)$ of the poset $P$ generated by $R$ has a complex zero that is not real.

results.title: Graphs that are line graphs
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A simple graph $G$ on a finite vertex type is a line graph if there are a natural number $k$ and a simple graph $H$ on the vertex set $\{0, \dots, k-1\}$ such that $G$ is isomorphic to the line graph $L(H)$. Here $L(H)$ has the edges of $H$ as its vertices, and two distinct edges of $H$ are adjacent in $L(H)$ when they share an endpoint.

results.title: Lexicographic product of graphs
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Given simple graphs $X$ and $Y$, the *lexicographic product* $X[Y]$ of $X$ and $Y$ is the simple graph with vertex set $V(X) \times V(Y)$ in which two vertices $(x_1, y_1)$ and $(x_2, y_2)$ are adjacent exactly when $x_1$ and $x_2$ are adjacent in $X$, or $x_1 = x_2$ and $y_1$ and $y_2$ are adjacent in $Y$.

For every $n$, in the $\mathrm{TM1}$ emulator of $M$, the configuration in the return state (for a given continuation), with internal state $v$ and head $n$ cells to the right of the bottom marker of $L$, reaches in exactly $n$ steps the same configuration with the head at the bottom marker.

If the $\mathrm{TM1}$ emulator of $M$ goes from $c$ to $c'$ in exactly $m$ steps, then the single-tape emulation of $M$ goes from the single-tape form of $c$ to the single-tape form of $c'$ in at most $3m$ steps.

results.title: Grouped y-fast trie
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: For natural numbers $w$ and $B$, a grouped y-fast trie over $w$-bit keys with group bound $B$ consists of an x-fast trie over $w$-bit keys, which holds the representatives, and a list of groups, each a list of $w$-bit keys. The structure itself imposes no condition on these fields; the intended invariants (the representative trie is a valid x-fast trie whose keys are exactly the group maxima, every group is…

results.title: Keys of a grouped y-fast trie
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The key set of a grouped y-fast trie $t$ is the finite set of all keys that occur in some group of $t$.

results.title: Stored keys are the keys of the groups
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every grouped y-fast trie $t$ over $w$-bit keys and every key $x$, $x$ lies in the contents of $t$ if and only if $x$ belongs to some group of $t$.

results.title: Ordered list of groups
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A list of groups, each a list of $w$-bit keys, is group ordered when every key of an earlier group is smaller than every key of a later group.

results.title: Validity of a grouped y-fast trie
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A grouped y-fast trie $t$ over keys in $\{0, \dots, 2^w - 1\}$ with group bound $B$ is valid when its representative trie is a valid x-fast trie; a key $r$ is stored in the representative trie exactly when $r$ is the last element of some group of $t$; every group of $t$ is nonempty, has at most $B$ keys, and is strictly increasing; and the groups of $t$ are ordered, that is, every key of an earlier group is smaller…

results.title: Group of a representative
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a grouped y-fast trie $t$ and a key $r$, the group of $r$ is the first group of $t$, in the order of the groups, whose last element is $r$, or the empty list if no group of $t$ ends with $r$.

results.title: Least representative at or above a key
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a grouped y-fast trie $t$ and a key $x$, the result is $x$ itself if the membership test of the representative x-fast trie of $t$ (a single probe of its deepest level) reports $x$ as present. Otherwise it is the successor of $x$ in the representative x-fast trie, that is, the least representative greater than $x$, or nothing if there is none.

results.title: Membership query of a grouped y-fast trie
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Given a grouped y-fast trie $t$ over $w$-bit keys and a key $x$, the query first finds a representative $r$: $r = x$ if the membership probe of the representative x-fast trie accepts $x$, and otherwise $r$ is the successor of $x$ in the representative trie. If there is no such $r$, the query returns false. Otherwise it returns whether $x$ belongs to the group owned by $r$, namely the first group of $t$ whose last…

results.title: Correctness of the y-fast trie membership query
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $t$ be a valid grouped y-fast trie over $w$-bit keys. Then for every key $x$, the membership query on $t$ (locate the least representative at least $x$, then scan its group) returns true at $x$ if and only if $x$ lies in the contents of $t$.

results.title: Successor query in a grouped y-fast trie
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a grouped y-fast trie $t$ and a key $x$, let $r$ be the least key greater than $x$ stored in the representative x-fast trie of $t$; if there is none, the query returns nothing. Otherwise let $g$ be the first group of $t$ whose last element is $r$, or the empty list if no group has last element $r$. The query then returns the first key of $g$ greater than $x$, or nothing if $g$ has no such key.

results.title: Successor query returns the least larger stored key
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $t$ be a valid grouped y-fast trie and let $x$, $y$ be keys. The successor query for $x$ in $t$ returns $y$ if and only if $y$ is stored in $t$, $x < y$, and $y \le z$ for every key $z$ stored in $t$ with $x < z$.

results.title: Successor query fails exactly when no larger key is stored
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $t$ be a valid grouped y-fast trie and $x$ a key. The successor query for $x$ in $t$ returns nothing if and only if no key stored in $t$ is greater than $x$.

results.title: The empty grouped y-fast trie
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For every key length $w$ and group bound $B$, the empty grouped y-fast trie has the empty x-fast trie as its trie of representatives and has no groups.

results.title: The empty grouped y-fast trie is valid
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every key width $w$ and group bound $B$, the empty grouped y-fast trie satisfies the grouped y-fast trie invariant.

results.title: The empty grouped y-fast trie has no members
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For all natural numbers $w$ and $B$ and every $w$-bit key $x$, the membership query on the empty grouped y-fast trie over $w$-bit keys with group bound $B$ returns false at $x$.

results.title: The empty grouped y-fast trie has no successors
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every key $x$, the successor query for $x$ in the empty grouped y-fast trie returns nothing.

results.title: Representative trie of a list
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a list $rs$ of $w$-bit keys, the representative x-fast trie of $rs$ is obtained from the empty x-fast trie over $w$-bit keys by inserting the elements of $rs$ one at a time, from first to last.

results.title: Inserting a list of keys into the empty x-fast trie gives a valid trie
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every list of $w$-bit keys, the x-fast trie obtained from the empty x-fast trie by inserting the keys of the list one at a time satisfies the x-fast trie invariant: each level holds exactly the prefixes of that length of the stored keys.

results.title: Keys of the trie of representatives
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every list $L$ of $w$-bit keys, the x-fast trie obtained by inserting the elements of $L$ one by one into the empty x-fast trie stores exactly the elements of $L$: its key set is the set of elements of $L$.

results.title: Grouped y-fast trie from a list of groups
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a list of groups $g_1, \dots, g_k$, each a list of $w$-bit keys, and any group-size bound $B$, this is the grouped y-fast trie whose groups are $g_1, \dots, g_k$ in this order and whose representative x-fast trie is obtained from the empty x-fast trie by inserting the last element of each nonempty group, in order. No condition on the groups is checked here; when a group is sorted, its last element is its maximum.

results.title: Assembling a valid grouped y-fast trie from groups
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $w$ and $B$ be natural numbers and let $g_1, \dots, g_k$ be a list of groups, each a list of keys in $\{0, \dots, 2^w - 1\}$. Suppose every group is nonempty, has at most $B$ keys, and is strictly increasing, and the groups are ordered: every key of an earlier group is smaller than every key of a later group. Then the grouped y-fast trie with group bound $B$ assembled from these groups, whose representatives…

results.title: Fuel-bounded chunking
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Given a bound $B$, a fuel $n$ and a list $l$ of $w$-bit keys, the fuel-bounded chunking is the empty list of chunks when $n = 0$ or $l$ is empty; otherwise it is the chunk formed by the first $\min(B, |l|)$ elements of $l$, followed by the fuel-bounded chunking with bound $B$ and fuel $n - 1$ of the remaining elements of $l$.

results.title: Chunking a list into groups
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Given a bound $B$ and a list $l$ of $w$-bit keys, when $B > 0$ the chunking of $l$ cuts $l$ from the left into consecutive chunks of exactly $B$ elements each, except that the last chunk holds the remaining one to $B$ elements; there are no chunks when $l$ is empty. When $B = 0$, the chunking has no chunks if $l$ is empty and is the single chunk $l$ otherwise.

results.title: Chunking with bound zero
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every nonempty list $l$ of $w$-bit keys, the chunking of $l$ with bound $B = 0$ consists of the single chunk $l$.

results.title: Chunking preserves the list
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every bound $B$ (including $B = 0$) and every list $l$ of $w$-bit keys, concatenating the chunks of the chunking of $l$ with bound $B$, in order, gives back $l$.

results.title: Chunks of a sorted list
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $B > 0$ and let $l$ be a strictly increasing list of $w$-bit keys. Then every chunk of the chunking of $l$ into groups of at most $B$ keys is nonempty, has at most $B$ elements, and is strictly increasing.

results.title: Chunks of a sorted list are ordered
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $B$ be a natural number and let $l$ be a strictly increasing list of $w$-bit keys. Then the chunk groups of $l$ with bound $B$ are group ordered: every key of an earlier chunk is smaller than every key of a later chunk.

results.title: Grouped y-fast trie from a sorted list
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a group bound $B$ and a list $l$ of $w$-bit keys, this is the grouped y-fast trie whose groups, in order, are consecutive pieces of $l$ that together make up $l$, and whose representative x-fast trie is obtained from the empty x-fast trie by inserting the last element of each group, in order. If $B > 0$, the groups are obtained by repeatedly cutting off the first $B$ keys, so every group has exactly $B$ keys…

results.title: Building from a sorted list gives a valid grouped y-fast trie
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $w$ and $B$ be natural numbers with $0 < B$, and let $l$ be a strictly increasing list of keys in $\{0, \dots, 2^w - 1\}$. Then the grouped y-fast trie with group bound $B$ built from $l$ by cutting it into consecutive groups of at most $B$ keys is valid.

results.title: Building from a nonempty list with group bound zero gives an invalid trie
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $w$ and every nonempty list $l$ of $w$-bit keys, the grouped y-fast trie with group bound $B = 0$ built from $l$ is not valid.

results.title: Keys of the grouped y-fast trie built from a list
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every group bound $B$ (including $B = 0$) and every list $l$ of $w$-bit keys, sorted or not, the key set of the grouped y-fast trie built from $l$ with group bound $B$ is exactly the set of elements of $l$.

results.title: Membership in a trie built from a sorted list
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $B > 0$ and let $l$ be a strictly increasing list of $w$-bit keys. Then for every key $x$, the membership query on the grouped y-fast trie built from $l$ with group bound $B$ returns true at $x$ if and only if $x$ belongs to $l$.

results.title: Successor in the trie built from a sorted list
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $B > 0$, let $l$ be a strictly increasing list of $w$-bit keys, and let $x$, $y$ be keys. The successor query for $x$ in the grouped y-fast trie built from $l$ with group bound $B$ returns $y$ if and only if $y$ belongs to $l$, $x < y$, and $y \le z$ for every $z$ in $l$ with $x < z$.
